entries.title: Ghost Gum, MacDonnell Range, near Alice Springs, Central Australia; EGOOTA (two watercolours sold as one lot)
entries.note: Lot 25. Two Rex Battarbee watercolours in one lot: a ghost gum landscape and one titled EGOOTA. Lot text: each signed lower right, the latter (Egoota) dated 1957, each signed and titled verso, 'See illustration of each'. Estimate CAD 700-900 for the pair. The Invaluable lot page shows no result. The search list's 'Sold: Upgrade subscription to view' label appears on every past lot, including ones that passed, so it proves nothing. The lot page dates it 17 Nov 2003; the search list says 18 Nov 2003. No image on Invaluable, and the lot text does not describe the Egoota subject. The title and year match Andy's painting and the size is similar (41.4 x 51.6 against about 38 x 50, which may be a sight size), so this is probably the same painting, offered in Canada in 2003 alongside a landscape. The reference file has the ghost gum half of this lot (Artnet, 2003-11-18, 41.4 x 51.6 cm) but not the Egoota half. Not checked: Waddington's own online archive, which may have the image and the price realised. Re-checked on 7 Nov 2026 by a second fetch of the Invaluable lot page: 'Two watercolours; each signed lower right, the latter dated 1957, each signed and titled verso ... Each approximately 16.3in x 20.3in - 41.4 x 51.6 cm. See illustration of each'. Sale name 'Art, Collectables'. No price or result shown.

entries.title: CONTEST FOR PAINTINGS
entries.note: The only call-for-entries notice found, for the first (1957) competition. Quoted from Trove OCR with obvious OCR slips corrected: 'Entries have opened for the Maude Vizard-Wholohan art prizes competition, run by the Royal South Australian Society of Arts. Prize-money is £300 for a landscape or seascape in oils, £100 for a water-colour (any subject), and £25 for a print (any subject). Entries close on June 14. The competition is open to Australian-born artists and artists who have lived in Australia for three years before the closing date. The entries must be original and must have been done in the 18 months before June 14.' This shows a watercolour class of any subject (so a portrait qualified) and an 18-month painting window. No judges are named. Note: the full article is copyright-blocked on Trove ('still within its copyright period'); the wording was checked on 7 Nov 2026 through Trove search snippets, which show '... in oils, £100 for a [water-colour] (any subject), and £25 for a print (any subject)', '... close on June 14. The competition is open to ... artists who have lived in ...' and 'The entries must be original and must have been done ...'.

entries.title: Worth Reporting (item 'An art prize with memories')
entries.venue: Australian Women's Weekly, p. 31, via Trove
entries.note: Confirms 1957 was the first contest. Quote: 'YOUTHFUL memories were revived for well-known Australian artist Hans Heysen when he was recently awarded second prize in the first Maude Vizard-Wholohan Art Contest, held in Adelaide.' Also: 'First prize went to South Australian Louis James, now living in London, and third prize to Murray Griffin, of Victoria, a Japanese P.O.W. during World War II.' It does not say which category each prize was. It wrongly says Mrs Wholohan died in 1951 and left the money to the Royal S.A. Society of Arts. No Battarbee mention.

entries.title: Artbursts: The Hiroshima Panels (includes section 'Adelaide Shows'), by Geoffrey Dutton
entries.venue: The Bulletin (Sydney), v.79 no.4091, pp. 24-25, via Trove digitised magazines
entries.note: Review of the 1958 prizes, read from the page OCR (nla.obj-687016450 and nla.obj-687016718). Quote: 'The South Australian Maude Vizard-Wholohan art-competitions for an oil of figures, a watercolor and a print offer really substantial prize-money, which this year attracted many inter-State entries. The S.A. judges, with an impartiality admirable but perhaps excessive, awarded the oil prize to Clifton Pugh, of Victoria, the watercolor to Hector Gilliland, of N.S.W., and the print to another Victorian, Lesbia Thorpe.' This confirms a 1958 watercolour category. Other exhibitors named: J. Carington Smith, Charles Bush, Margarita Stipnieks, Juta Puust. Battarbee is not mentioned. Judges' names and prize amounts are not given.

entries.title: The Maude Vizard-Wholohan Art Prizes 1957 (exhibition review)
entries.venue: Bulletin of the National Gallery of South Australia, vol. 19 no. 1, cited by Australian Prints + Printmaking
entries.note: Abstract only: 'The first Maude Vizard-Wholohan award.' It mentions only the £25 print prize, won by Murray Griffin (ill.). Author and pages not given. The full Bulletin text was not found online. A July 1957 review means the 1957 judging was over by July 1957, which fits the 14 June 1957 closing date.

entries.title: The Maude Vizard-Wholohan Art Prizes [1958] (exhibition review)
entries.venue: Bulletin of the National Gallery of South Australia, vol. 20 no. 1, cited by Australian Prints + Printmaking
entries.note: Abstract only: 'Print prize (£25) won by Lesbia Thorpe (ill.).' Its artist link points to Hall Thorpe in error. Watercolour entries and the hanging list are not described.

entries.title: Valuable Art Prize Bequest
entries.note: Terms of the original will. Quote: 'An art prize worth £200 to be offered annually by the SA National Gallery and SA Royal Society of Arts is provided for by a substantial bequest from the estate of the late Mrs. F. Wholohan, who died on September 7, aged 91.' Also: 'Competitors must have lived in Australia for at least seven consecutive years before the date of the competition.' The subjects were to alternate each year, 'one year a portrait and the following year a landscape or seascape.' The winning picture was to become the property of the National Gallery and hang with the artist's name, 'and later to be sent to a country institute.'

entries.title: Views differ on art prize
entries.note: Quote: 'The prize will be offered annually by the SA National Gallery and the SA Royal Society of Arts.' Also: 'Included in the conditions of the prize are that the winner must have resided for at least seven consecutive years in Australia, and that the subject of the paintings shall alternate from year to year, one year a portrait, the next a landscape or seascape.' The second quote is OCR-tidied, and the dash in the original is rendered as a comma.

entries.title: Family Notices (death notice of Elizabeth Maude Wholohan)
entries.note: Death date. Quote (OCR-tidied): 'WHOLOHAN. On September 7, at residence, 3 Webb street, Rose Park, Elizabeth Maude, beloved wife of the late Frank F. Wholohan, and loving daughter of the late Joseph and Eliza Vizard. Aged 90 years.' The Advertiser of 27 Sept 1950 gives her age as 91.

entries.title: RULING SOUGHT ON £10,000 ART GIFT
entries.note: The trust was in court at the end of 1954. Quote (OCR-tidied): 'Mrs. Wholohan's will said that the SA Art Gallery Board were, with an outside art group, to administer the trust and that the winning painting must be hung for 12 months in the gallery. Before Mr. Justice Mayo it was revealed today that the Art Gallery Board are disclaiming the trust.' The executors were Bagot's Executor and Trustee Co. Ltd.

entries.title: Supreme Court, Civil Sittings (item 'Art Bequest In Doubt')
entries.note: Quote: 'By her 1947 will Mrs. Wholohan, who died in September, 1950, gave the residuary estate to the Board for the promotion of the art of painting and to provide a £200 annual Maude Vizard-Wholohan Art Prize, and to hang the winning picture in the National Gallery for at least one year.' Also: 'The Society of Arts might be able to execute the trust.' The case was 'Part heard and adjourned'. No report of the final ruling was found on Trove.

entries.title: The Ghan Goes North
entries.note: Shows Battarbee painting named tribesman portraits in Alice Springs in late 1956, the year before Egoota is dated. Caption (raw OCR): 'Agar Nabi a Pintulii tribesman, from an original waterrolor by Rex Battarbee.' This reads as Pintubi and watercolor. The text says that near Billy Goat Hill 'an artist, founder of the School of Aboriginal Art, is painting portraits'. The title pattern is the same as 'Egoota (Pitjantjara tribesman)'.

entries.title: 'Nabi, Puntubi Tribesman' (1940) watercolour by Rex Battarbee (born 1893)
entries.venue: AIATSIS Photographic collection (J. V. S. Megaw, MEGAW.J01.CS-000095611), via Trove
entries.note: A Battarbee bust portrait of a named man from a Western Desert group, titled the same way as Egoota. It is the same sitter as the 1956 Chronicle caption. Size not given. This was the only Trove image hit for 'Battarbee tribesman'.

entries.title: Portrait of Richard Moketarinja
entries.note: A Battarbee watercolour portrait of an Aboriginal man, 'watercolour on paper'. Donated in 2024 through the Cultural Gifts Program by Dr Beverley and Mr Alan Castleman. Size not given on Trove. A comparable portrait from the 1950s.

entries.title: Native Study
entries.note: Quote: 'YALATOOQULPA, of the Ngalia tribe. This portrait study of an aboriginal is one of the works of Rex Battarbee, whose exhibition of Central Australian watercolors is now being held at the Society of Arts Gallery.' This shows that Battarbee had shown named tribal portraits with the (Royal) SA Society of Arts in Adelaide well before the prize existed.

entries.title: CENTRAL AUSTRALIA ON CANVAS
entries.note: Quote: 'Mr. Battarbee shows also a few native head portraits, which are clean and expressive, and form a valuable record of aboriginal life.' Shows that head-and-shoulders Aboriginal portraits were a long-running sideline for him.

entries.title: Advertising (Tmara-Mara Galleries, no street given)
entries.venue: Centralian Advocate (Alice Springs), p. 10, via Trove
entries.note: A typical 1956 ad with no street address. Quote: 'TMARA - MARA GALLERIES Open for inspection of Works of Art WEDNESDAY AND SATURDAY, otherwise by appointment. Also obtainable - Prints from Originals - by - ALBERT NAMATJIRA, REX BATTARBEE, ABORIGINAL ARTISTS. REX BATTARBEE, Phone 220.' The same ad on the same page names 'THE FARM SHOP STURT TERRACE. EAST SIDE', which shows Sturt Terrace is on Alice Springs' East Side.

entries.title: Advertising (Tmara-Mara Galleries, last style without street)
entries.note: Quote: 'Tmara-Mara Galleries OPEN FOR INSPECTION OF WORKS OF ART. WEDNESDAY' (Wednesday and Saturday opening, no street). The ads keep this wording up to 31 Jan 1958.

entries.title: Advertising (Tmara-Mara Galleries, Sturt Terrace)
entries.note: Quote: 'Tmara-Mara Galleries STURT TERRACE MONDAY TO SATURDAY'. The same new wording first appears in the 14 Feb 1958 issue, which is the earliest Trove ad giving Sturt Terrace. It comes with 'REX BATTARBEE (ARTIST) - PHONE 220.' The change in early 1958 to a street address and six-day opening suggests the gallery-home at Sturt Terrace was new or newly advertised at that point. Re-checked 7 Nov 2026 with a Trove search sorted by date: the earliest Tmara-Mara ad giving 'STURT TERRACE' is 14 Feb 1958, p. 5; the 1956 ads that mention Sturt Terrace belong to The Farm Shop, a different business.

entries.title: Advertising (Rex Battarbee, Sturt Terrace)
entries.note: Quote: 'TMARA-MARA GALLERIES. REX BATTARBEE, STURT TERRACE. PHONE 220'. From 27 June 1958 the ads also read 'REX BATTARBEE (ARTIST) PHONE 220. STURT TERRACE'. No house number (6) appears in any Trove item found.

entries.title: WATER SUPPLY TO BE SUPPLEMENTED
entries.venue: Centralian Advocate (Alice Springs), p. 6, via Trove
entries.note: Raw OCR: 'A test note on tne east name ot tne loaa Kiver, near Mr. Battarbee's residence, has proved that a suitable supply exists there'. This reads as a test hole on the east bank of the Todd River. So by April 1957 his home was on the east side of the Todd, the same side as Sturt Terrace. This means he may already have been living on or near Sturt Terrace before the 1958 ads, so the address alone does not settle the label year.

entries.title: NEW BOOK ON SALE SOON: ART OF REX BATTARBEE
entries.venue: Centralian Advocate (Alice Springs), p. 19, via Trove
entries.note: Announces Strehlow's Legend Press book on Battarbee. Quote: 'Incidentally, Battarbee is having an exhibition at the moment, and details of this will be found on another page in this issue.' That exhibition report was not found by Trove search, probably because of OCR. No mention of portraits or the prize.

entries.title: Maude Vizard-Wholohan Art Prizes Exhibition (annual catalogue series)
entries.venue: Art Gallery of NSW Research Library, via Trove (Libraries Australia ID 26515531)
entries.note: This is the best lead to a 1958 list of hung entries. It is an annual series of exhibition catalogues, 'v. ; 21-23 cm'. Trove does not show which years AGNSW holds. Trove has separately catalogued RSASA catalogues only for 1964 (work 249071072) and 1968. No 1957 or 1958 catalogue appears as a separate record in Trove or in the SLSA catalogue.

entries.title: SLSA catalogue word search 'Wholohan' (12 results)
entries.venue: State Library of South Australia catalogue
entries.note: No 1957 or 1958 prize catalogue. Hits are later purchase-award catalogues (1976 onwards), two citations, Hinds PRG 1673, and Ostoja-Kotkowski papers PRG 919/39 'Art exhibitions' 1955-1993, which could include RSASA prize ephemera. A 'Battarbee' search (13 results) gave books only, including Strehlow's 'Rex Battarbee: artist and founder of the Aboriginal art movement in central Australia' and Quarmby and McGregor's 'Rex Battarbee: artist & Albert Namatjira's friend'. Neither is online.

entries.title: Maude Vizard-Wholohan Art Prize Exhibition 1959
entries.venue: Australian Prints + Printmaking exhibition record (Royal South Australian Society of Arts Gallery)
entries.note: Shows the prize exhibition was hung at the RSASA Gallery in 1959. The site also has a 1960 record at the RSASA Gallery (exhibitions/4059) and a 1962 record at the National Gallery of SA (exhibitions/1995). No 1957 or 1958 exhibition record was found there. The site's search page did not render.

entries.title: Katinggura
entries.venue: Art Gallery of South Australia, Adelaide
entries.note: Watercolour on paper. Accession 20001P2. Credit: A.M. and A.R. Ragless Bequest Funds 2000. Place made: Hermannsburg, NT. The page records it as signed and dated lower right 'REX BATTARBEE _ 1938', the same signature layout as Egoota. The page does not name or describe the sitter (the title may be his name, but the page does not say so). Image URL: https://agsa-prod.s3.amazonaws.com/media/dd/images/69013-HQ-20001P2.a6caab1.jpg. I viewed the image. It is a bust-length bearded Aboriginal man in three-quarter view looking to the viewer's left, set right of centre against a big plain sky with a low horizon of rocks. That is the same compositional formula and almost the same sheet format as Egoota (38 x 50). Differences: long twisted, forked beard; hair tied up in a bun bound with a thin yellow hair-string, not a red band; pale cream sky, not blue; low pink-grey rocks and green spinifex along the bottom edge instead of a red rock face and distant hills. Lined forehead and stern sideways look are similar. In my view this is not the same man. He does look like the sitter in the 1942 'Arunta Tribal Elder' (bun, yellow string, long forked beard), which would suggest Battarbee repainted the same sitters years apart, but that is my visual impression only. Apart from Warrnambool's Munduckinera, this is the only Battarbee portrait of an Aboriginal person I found in a public collection online.

entries.title: Uncovering a legacy: a daughter's quest to track down her father's paintings
entries.note: Headline as shown when fetched (the URL slug is worded differently). Published 7:00am 15 Aug 2025, updated 10:41am the same day. A subscription prompt shows, but the fetched text ran to the end of the story. Gayle Quarmby (nee Battarbee) is asking the public to help find her father's lost paintings, especially early works from the 1920s to 1940 that she thinks may still be around the Warrnambool district. She is "penning a book about her father's life and art", with a Warrnambool launch planned later in 2025. The article puts his complete output at about 700 paintings. The only contact route given is the email quarmbyhort@gmail.com. No website, Facebook page or publisher is named. It mentions the 1956 portrait Munduckinera, Pintubi Tribesman at Warrnambool Art Gallery, describing the sitter as a first-contact Aboriginal man, and says other works are in national and private collections. There is no mention of a register, database or catalogue raisonne, or of Egoota, the Pitjantjatjara or the Maud Vizard-Wholohan prize. I found no syndicated copy or other coverage of the appeal in two searches.

entries.title: Modern Australian Aboriginal Art, by Rex Battarbee (Angus & Robertson), Internet Archive copy
entries.date: 1958 (as shown; a reprint of the 1951 book)
entries.note: I did not borrow it, because that needs a login. I used the free search-inside on the OCR text. The contents page (n6) lists a Foreword, an Introduction, then chapters on Albert Namatjira, Edwin, Otto and Reuben Pareroultja, Walter Ebatarinja, Enos and Oskar Namatjira, Henoch Raberaba, Richard Moketarinja and Ewald Namatjira. The Coloured Plates list (n7, 21 plates) is grouped under those Aboriginal artists' names, and every legible title is a landscape. The Other Illustrations list (n8) is black-and-white photographs of the artists and the mission. 'Battarbee' appears only on the title page, in the foreword (pp. 6-7) and on p. 51. Egoota, tribesman, Pitjantjara and Pitjantjatjara each return zero hits. 'Portrait' appears once (p. 93, not about a portrait). So the book does not reproduce his own portraits, and Egoota is not in it. Caveats: this was an OCR search only, and the title of plate VIII was not visible.

entries.title: Modern Australian Aboriginal Art, limited deluxe edition signed by the artists (bookseller listing)
entries.note: The deluxe issue is limited to 130 numbered copies (this one is no. 15). It is signed by Battarbee and ten Hermannsburg artists, with a foreword by T.G.H. Strehlow. It has 23 tipped-in colour plates including the frontispiece (two more than the trade edition) and 12 black-and-white plates. The listing gives no plate list and does not mention Battarbee's own portraits, a tribesman or the Pitjantjatjara. The asking price is AUD 5,500, which I left out of the price fields because it is for the book, not a painting. A biblio.co.nz listing of the 1958 reprint gives 55 pages plus 21 colour plates. The University of Melbourne's Menzies Collection holds deluxe copy no. 45 (https://www.menziescollection.esrc.unimelb.edu.au/biogs/E002115b.htm).

entries.title: Rex Batterbee paintings (photo PH0815/0092)
entries.venue: Library & Archives NT, Territory Stories (Alice Springs Public Library Collection, PictureNT)
entries.note: Photograph by Audrey Attwood. The description says it shows paintings by Rex Batterbee (spelt that way) at his residence in Alice Springs. No sitters or portraits are mentioned. The page thumbnail shows framed paintings on a wall that look like landscapes, and no portrait is visible at thumbnail size. I did not open the full image because the page showed a cultural advisory and a cookie overlay with only an OK button, and I did not accept it. Andy could open it himself to see whether any portrait was hanging in his house in 1963. I found no Battarbee photographs of Aboriginal sitters in Territory Stories in this pass.

entries.title: South Australian Museum Archives, Battarbee items (titles as shown in search results)
entries.note: Not opened. The search results showed these titles: 'Artsist Rex Batterbee and his Pupils.' (AA 780/1/151); 'Sales from Battarbee (See AA 663) listsof paintings' (AA 662/103/39, https://www.samuseum.sa.gov.au/collection/archives/provenances/series/items/aa-662-103-39); 'Sales Liselle Tohlhgen, Rex Battarbee (See AA 663)' (AA 662/103/18, https://samuseum.sa.gov.au/collection/archives/provenances/series/items/aa-662-103-18); and a photo of Battarbee painting towards Mt Hermannsburg across the Finke River (AA 662/77/9). The sales lists might record his own sales, but nothing shown links them to portraits or Egoota. Possible follow-up.

entries.title: Modern Aboriginal Paintings, by Rex Battarbee (Rigby, Adelaide)
entries.note: A separate, later book: 32 pages, 42 scanned images. Booksellers' search results credit Rex and Bernice Battarbee. I did not search inside it because of the budget. It could be checked for reproductions of his own portraits.
